vertical-cultural.source: Wikimedia Commons via Flickr — humdingor, "Diwali Decor"
vertical-cultural.altText: Rows of lit clay diyas arranged on the floor beneath a silver tray of floating flowers and candles for Diwali
vertical-cultural.note: Lit clay diyas and a floating-flower tray — a genuine Diwali decoration setup, matches Special & Cultural festivals.

vertical-destination.altText: Umaid Bhawan Palace in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, a sandstone palace with a large central dome
vertical-destination.note: Umaid Bhawan Palace, Jodhpur, Rajasthan — a real, iconic Indian destination-wedding venue.

wedding-cultural-north-indian.source: Wikimedia Commons — iMahesh, "Indian Wedding Ritual - Jaimala or Varmala (01)"
wedding-cultural-north-indian.altText: A Hindu bride and groom exchanging floral garlands during the jaimala ritual, mandap decorated with fairy lights behind them
wedding-cultural-north-indian.note: Jaimala/varmala is the ritual most associated with North Indian Hindu weddings specifically, distinguishing it from the South Indian and Bengali ceremony styles sourced separately.

wedding-cultural-south-indian.source: Wikimedia Commons — Kritzolina, "Wedding ceremony in Tamil Nadu 01"
wedding-cultural-south-indian.altText: A Tamil Hindu bride in a red and gold silk saree performing a traditional ritual with her seated parents
wedding-cultural-south-indian.note: Genuine Tamil Nadu wedding ritual, distinct ceremony style and attire from North Indian weddings.

wedding-cultural-punjabi.source: Wikimedia Commons — Japleenpasricha, "Sikh wedding ceremony in a Gurudwara"
wedding-cultural-punjabi.altText: A Sikh bride and groom facing the Guru Granth Sahib under a gold canopy in a Gurudwara
wedding-cultural-punjabi.note: Unambiguously Sikh/Punjabi — Guru Granth Sahib and Ik Onkar symbol visible in a Gurudwara setting.

wedding-cultural-bengali.source: Wikimedia Commons — Goutam1962, "Portrait of a Bengali Bride 01"
wedding-cultural-bengali.altText: A Bengali bride in a red and gold Benarasi saree with a sheer red veil, gold jewelry and a nose ring
wedding-cultural-bengali.note: Distinctive Bengali bridal styling — red Benarasi saree, nath (nose ring), red chandan forehead pattern.

wedding-cultural-rajasthani.source: Wikimedia Commons — Prithvipalsinghrathore, "Rajasthani Bride in Traditional Attire"
wedding-cultural-rajasthani.altText: A Rajasthani bride in a red gota-patti embroidered lehenga in front of a colourful bandhani textile backdrop
wedding-cultural-rajasthani.note: Distinctly Rajasthani gota-patti embroidery and bandhani/patchwork textile setting.

wedding-cultural-gujarati.source: Wikimedia Commons — Yann Forget, "Hindu Bride, Ahmedabad, Gujarat" (Commons Featured Picture)
wedding-cultural-gujarati.altText: A Gujarati bride in red and green panetar bridal wear holding a ceremonial copper kalash topped with a coconut
wedding-cultural-gujarati.note: Panetar-style bridal wear and the kalash ritual are specifically Gujarati.

wedding-cultural-muslim.altText: A groom in a gold sherwani during a Nikah ceremony, surrounded by men in white kurtas and topi caps as the marriage contract is signed
wedding-cultural-muslim.note: Unambiguous Nikah ceremony imagery — marriage contract signing, topi caps, no visual ambiguity with a Hindu ceremony.

wedding-cultural-christian.source: Wikimedia Commons — Nikhil Jose 7, "Kerala Christian Wedding"
wedding-cultural-christian.altText: A Kerala Christian bride in a cream saree and groom in a dark suit walking under an umbrella with tropical palm trees behind them
wedding-cultural-christian.note: Cream saree bridal colour and Western-suit groom attire are distinctly Kerala Christian, not Hindu-red.
